title: when history itself is the problem
goal: D2 Big files, leaked secrets, and rewriting a whole repository
startWith: A throwaway clone. Never a first attempt on anything shared.

newIdeas.plain: The supported tool for bulk history rewriting. filter-branch is deprecated and slow.
Clone less: --filter=blob:none for metadata first, --depth for recent history only.
Large files stored outside the object database, with a stub committed in their place.

tasks.do: Find what is making the repository big

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git count-objects -vH
git rev-list --objects --all \
  | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype) %(objectname) %(objectsize) %(rest)' \
  | awk '$1=="blob"' | sort -k3 -n -r | head -20

tasks.do: Purge a leaked secret from history — and know what that does not fix
tasks.why: Rewriting changes every downstream hash. The credential is still compromised and must be rotated regardless.

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
pip install git-filter-repo
git filter-repo --invert-paths --path secrets.env
# every collaborator must re-clone; every open PR is invalidated
# rotate the credential anyway: it was public

tasks.do: Clone big repositories without waiting for all of history

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git clone --filter=blob:none <url>    # blobs fetched on demand
git clone --depth 1 <url>             # latest snapshot only
git fetch --unshallow                 # fill it in later

tasks.do: Track a large binary with LFS

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git lfs install
git lfs track "*.pdf"
git add .gitattributes && git commit -m "track pdfs with lfs"
git lfs ls-files

tasks.do: Maintain a repository that has grown slow

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git maintenance start              # background gc, prefetch, commit-graph
git gc --prune=now --aggressive    # one-off, slow
git fsck --lost-found              # find dangling objects

proof.note: You rewrote a repository knowingly, fallout included.

doneWhen: You can rewrite history when it is genuinely the answer, and you know why it usually is not.
